summary: Stage 2 is implemented within the agreed scope and the supplied evidence is consistent with the code. adapter.py consumes the generic (jungfrau, sim10, seed) field through BatchFieldDescriptor rows whose ABI (FIELD_* columns, LOC_* locator columns, STATUS_FOUND) is imported from the live framework modules and substituted into the kernel with delimited tokens; the kernel checks SOURCE_PRESENT, null pointers, type 1/rank 1/element size 2, locator status/type/rank/dim0/nbytes, and offset+extent against the input base size before any dereference, and reads uint16 words bytewise so odd offsets are safe. Locator offsets are relative to the same per-group raw base that the framework writes into FIELD_RAW_PTR (walk_xtc/locate_fields use input_bases per dgram), so the pointer arithmetic is coherent for bulk-read groups. Raw and error outputs are published and presence is kept alive before the launch; the unchanged jungfrau_calibration.py publishes its output before its launch; all work is on the supplied stream and no borrowed descriptor is retained past the callback. Physical panel identity is preserved: canonical segment ids are asserted equal to 0..31 and passed unchanged to the calibration kernel's segment map against full (3,32,512,1024) constants. The expansion is a materialized contiguous uint16 (N,32,512,1024) array, not a broadcast view. The hardened writer closes F-002 (Shapes-before-Data require at fixture.py:134, tested) and F-004 (verify.check_provenance binds generation.json code/manifest hashes to the imported writer, helper and frozen manifest, tested); F-003 is documented and the GPU task does not read the unaligned scalars; F-005 is moot since review-01/ exists. The schedule keeps the native prefix and SlowUpdates, uses the source's own Disable/EndStep/EndRun as templates for truncated prefixes, and emits the actual closing transitions for the tail window; it enforces exactly one native step. verify.py independently re-decodes source and output, compares seeds to raw[::10], checks scalars, non-JF leaves, SMD offset rewrites, trace offsets, ten identical timelines, the transition state machine, EOF and a serial DataSource traversal. gpu_accept.py compares every expanded raw word and every calibrated float32 bit against CPU v3 driven with nda_raw and the same frozen constants, with the constructor-scoped RunSerial loader override limited to the test DataSource. Summary evidence (8 unit tests; 10/3/1000 events; 320/96/32,000 panel checks; callback size counts 3,3,3,1 / 2,1 / {7:92,6:51,5:7,2:7,1:1}=158 calls and 1,000 events; two CUDA streams; ten device guard cases; all raw/calibrated bitwise equal; recorded CuPy 14.0.1 / KvikIO 26.10 / compat ON) is internally consistent with the code paths and with status.json job ids. Two low, non-blocking documentation/evidence inaccuracies are reported; no correctness or acceptance gap was found. No psana core files were inspected as changed and none of the examined framework modules differ from what the adapter assumes.
checks: Read all files in notes/mfx_expand10_stage2_20261105/ (README, scope, adapter.py, fixture.py, verify.py, gpu_accept.py, test_fixture.py, runtime.sh, run_gpu.sbatch, status.json, validation-summary.json, tiny-single-result.json, unit-tests.log, review-01/context.md) and the updated proposal synthetic_mfx_expand10.md.

Checked detector routing: register_reader sets detectors.jungfrau_sim10_1_0_0 so dgrammanager._setup_det_class_table places jungfrau in det_classes['normal'] and stream_id_to_detnames, satisfying ds_base.resolve_gpu_stream_ids exclusive-owner check; sim10meta has no class so it does not become a stream owner.

Checked CPU reference: calib_jungfrau_versions uses nda_raw when supplied, cversion=3, cmpars=None; det.raw._calibconst replaced with frozen (array, doc) dict; comparison is bitwise on uint32 views plus finiteness.

Checked schedule and verifier: schedule keeps all non-L1 rows up to last, native tail rows after last when the window ends at the source end, otherwise inserts 9/7/5 from source templates with ordered integer-ns timestamps; requires non-SlowUpdate/non-L1 services == [2,4,6,8,9,7,5]; verify enforces state machine, counts == [count], identical ten-stream timelines, EOF, and serial DataSource traversal with skip_calib_load='all'.

Confirmed F-002 closure (fixture.py:134 + test_shapes_after_data_rejected) and F-004 closure (verify.check_provenance + test_provenance_rejects_changed_writer_and_manifest); Stage 1 files not modified per scope (Stage 1 fixture.py/verify.py still present unchanged in the tree listing).

A one-event callback occurred, but it was not the final one; the final partial callback was six events. Tiny (final 1) and tail (final 1) are described correctly.

findings.evidence: All three fixture entries report "source_start_event": null, including the tail fixture that README describes as source indices 36034-36036. fixture.make writes an integer source_start_event into generation.json and verify.py requires it to be an int, so the null values indicate the summarizer read the wrong document (verification report rather than generation.json). The compact evidence therefore does not show that the tail fixture is the final three source events; that fact is only verifiable from the scratch generation.json, which this review could not read.
